local_entities.label: B'Elanna Torres under induced mating-bond effects

evidence.summary: Vorik proposes marriage to Torres, is rejected, and later initiates unwanted physical contact during worsening pon farr.
The Doctor identifies Vorik's life-threatening neurochemical pon farr condition and Tuvok describes culturally recognized resolution routes.
Tuvok and Vorik infer that Vorik's brief mating-bond contact transmitted a similar neurochemical state to Torres.
Torres shows escalating aggression, sexuality, territoriality, memory gaps and reduced self-control while still expressing preferences and resisting others' interpretations.
Paris acknowledges attraction to Torres but repeatedly refuses sexual contact while she is impaired, saying he will not take advantage of her altered judgment.
The Doctor uses a holographic Vulcan mate as a treatment for Vorik; his biochemical readings improve temporarily.
Hidden Sakari survivors say unknown invaders destroyed their surface colony and they have concealed themselves underground since then.
Vorik later challenges for Torres; Torres chooses to fight him herself, and ritual combat resolves both altered biochemical states.
Torres attributes much of her conduct to the induced chemical state while acknowledging unresolved attraction and embarrassment.
During cleanup, the Sakari and Voyager crew uncover a Borg corpse identified as one of the invaders.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: Vorik's pon farr is accidentally transmitted to Torres while an away team discovers a hidden colony and evidence of Borg attack.
neutral_coding.identity_agency: Altered biochemistry changes behavior without creating replacement persons or eliminating all agency.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Torres's later attribution to chemistry does not prove every feeling or statement during the episode was wholly foreign to her.
